cluster_name: Pope Leo XIV visits France, Paris mass draws 800,000, Lourdes abuse meeting
tldr: At the headline layer the global press splits sharply by region: Asian and African outlets (Philippines, Kenya, Nigeria, India, Malaysia/Singapore) lead almost unanimously with the clerical sex abuse accountability angle, while wire services, North American, and Gulf outlets foreground the 800,000-crowd spectacle. Breitbart is the single most editorially distinctive headline in the corpus, coupling crowd scale with 'Guillotine Terror Beheadings' to encode a Catholic counter-revolutionary frame absent from every other outlet. The AI 'paradise of machines' warning — prominent in body text — breaks through at headline level only across five outlets (Turkey, NPR/USA, India, Malaysia, South Africa), signalling that most editors treated it as a secondary story angle. Vatican News and Religion News Service maintain an entirely devotional register at title level, suppressing the abuse dimension visible in nearly every secular outlet's headline.
event_summary: Pope Leo XIV held a four-day visit to France including an open-air mass for approximately 800,000 people at Place de la Concorde in Paris on 26 September, followed by a private meeting with seven clerical sex abuse survivors at Lourdes on 27 September.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to embed 'Guillotine Terror Beheadings', coupling the 800,000-person crowd with the French Revolution's execution site — a civilizational counter-revolutionary frame invisible at the title layer of every other outlet in the corpus.
Only headline to link the visit to a looming French election ('as French election looms'), surfacing a political dimension entirely absent from every other outlet's title.

Both Vatican News headlines are exclusively devotional (Marian entrustment, pilgrim farewell) with no reference to the abuse scandal — the widest headline-layer divergence from the dominant accountability register across the corpus.

Only headline to position AI ethics and clergy abuse accountability as co-equal headline agenda items ('with AI, apologies for clergy abuse on agenda'), framing the visit as a progressive reform mission on simultaneous fronts.

bottom_line: At headline level, Pope Leo XIV's France visit resolves into two near-equal frames — 800,000-crowd as Catholic revival signal (wire services, Americas, Gulf) and clerical abuse moral reckoning (Asian and African outlets) — with Breitbart's 'Guillotine Terror Beheadings' headline standing as the corpus's single most editorially extreme title, encoding a counter-revolutionary civilizational frame absent from every other outlet. The pope's AI 'paradise of machines' warning, prominent in body text, surfaces at the headline layer only in five outliers, confirming it was deprioritised as front-page framing by the majority of editors.
